newsitem.title: USA: U.S. crudes end weak, sweet grades maintain levels.
newsitem.headline: U.S. crudes end weak, sweet grades maintain levels.

text.p: U.S. crudes ended the week lower, pressured on an outright basis by renewed selling in the futures market, traders said.
Domestic grade differentials saw sweet parcels maintain strength, while sour price levels retreated slightly.
Outright cash crude prices reflected new sentiment in the market that a bearish turn had taken place. NYMEX spot crude ended on the down side for the fifth consecutive session.
Active refiner demand allowed sweet grades to stay above a 70 cents premium to the West Texas Intermediate Cushing for Louisiana grades, as North Sea arbitrage remained uneconomic.
December West Texas Intermediate/Cushing ended at $22.95-$23.05 a barrel, down around 30 cts from Thursday's closing cash levels.
Iraq entered the news again, but developments at the United Nations failed to jostle prices Friday.

U.S. Ambassador Madeleine Albright said Iraq had made "outrageous demands" delaying implementation of the oil-for-food deal, in addition to destabilizing the north of the country by invading Kurdish regions in late August.
Albright spoke after the U.N. Security Council renewed broad sanctions against Iraq at the normal six-month review.
Values for grades saw Midland/WTI trade last at a 5 cts premium to the WTI/Cushing, talked at a plus 4-6 cts spread.
Light Louisiana Sweet/St. James was hovering between 70-75 cts Friday, selling at 72-74 cts over the WTI marker.
Heavy Louisiana Sweet/Empire was slightly firmer than the LLS, talked at 74-78 cts over WTI/Cushing, traders said.
Sours saw Eugene Island decline, down to a value of $1.18 under the WTI/Cushing. West Texas Sour/Midland slipped around 5 cts to trade at $1.50 below the WTI/Cushing.
December Postings Plus was sold late at $2.01, and talked into the late afternoon around $2.00-$2.05.
